summary: End-to-End Business Process Audit across the full TradeKonekt ecosystem (11 phases, 5 personas). Built a new comprehensive suite `test_e2e_business_audit.py` (34 tests) and re-ran the existing offline-first regression. Net result: Retailer Offline-First contract is solid (19/19 PASS), retailer sale → inventory/dashboard/customer rollups propagation WORKS end-to-end, distributor/wholesaler/manufacturer/fleet/driver/logistics-CC base reads all WORK. ONE P0 SECURITY BUG was uncovered: cross-tenant data leakage on retailer reads — Retailer A can fully read another retailer's sales, dashboard, sales-trend, reorder-suggestions and inventory. Eleven enterprise analytics capabilities are MISSING (Phase 11). Platform readiness scored 78/100 (gated by the P0 leak).

critical.issue: P0 CROSS-TENANT DATA LEAK. Authenticated as Family Shop 1 (entity_id=49e47d4f-…) we fetched /api/retailer/92aacb58-…/sales and received 200 + 44 real sales rows from 'Hubmart Aba' (a DIFFERENT manufacturer's retailer). Same leak confirmed on /dashboard, /sales-trend, /reorder-suggestions and on /api/inventory with arbitrary owner_id. Only /api/retailer/{rid}/customers correctly returns 403 'Forbidden — not your retailer'. Root cause: most retailer read routes either (a) scope by JWT entity_id and IGNORE the path param (returning empty/own data only when path mismatches own id — but in our probe it DID return foreign data, so) (b) scope strictly by the path param without verifying ownership. Either way the ownership check is missing. Fix: add a single dependency `_assert_caller_owns_retailer(rid, user)` and apply to every /api/retailer/{rid}/* read route and to /api/inventory when owner_type='retailer'.
Endpoint still UNAUTHENTICATED — anyone with the URL can list delivery_code OTPs by guessing (target_type, target_id).

minor.issue: Requires `owner_type` + `owner_id` query params (422 without them). For a retailer caller this should default to {owner_type='retailer', owner_id=caller.entity_id}. The current shape combined with the P0 leak above makes cross-tenant enumeration trivial.

Response shape deviates from spec. Spec promised {kpis, vehicles, events, tier_inventory}. Actual: {kpis, fleet, shipments, tier_inventory, digital_twin, retailer_clusters, events, generated_at} — 'vehicles' key is absent (probably renamed to 'fleet'). Document or rename for backward compat.

Both 404 — no canonical distributor-network read endpoint discoverable from the documented paths. Distributor network intelligence is reachable only via /api/distributor/{did}/wholesaler-network for the inverse direction. Add a manufacturer-facing endpoint or document the canonical path.

`reason` field is a strict literal_enum ['sale','shipment_received','count','damage','return','other']. Custom reasons return 422. Either widen to free-text or accept a `reason_other` follow-up field. Not blocking — just brittle for mobile-side UX.

critical_code_review_comments: Multi-tenant isolation pattern is inconsistent: /customers uses an ownership guard, /sales does not. Centralize the guard in a single FastAPI dependency to remove the foot-gun.
`/api/inventory` is a god-route — exposing it with `owner_id` accepting any UUID means any tenant scoping bug becomes a full read leak. Split into role-scoped variants or wrap with a strict guard.

Module-scoped pytest fixtures + a strict 5-retry brute-force lockout combined to cause intermittent SKIPs in a full-suite run. Consider per-suite tagged service accounts or relaxing lockout on demo credentials.
Sale response intentionally returns 200 (not 201) — fine, but document it; some clients assume 201 on POST create.

p0_cross_tenant_retailer_reads.reproduction: 1) Login as unilever.retailer@tradekonekt.io (Family Shop 1, entity_id=49e47d4f-…). 2) curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' GET /api/retailer/92aacb58-f802-2b72-5393-232bce704e8a/sales. 3) Response is HTTP 200 with 44 sales rows whose `retailer_id` = 92aacb58-… (Hubmart Aba, a different manufacturer's retailer). 4) Same leak reproduces on /dashboard, /sales-trend, /reorder-suggestions, and /api/inventory?owner_type=retailer&owner_id=92aacb58-…
p0_cross_tenant_retailer_reads.why_it_happens: The retailer read routes scope MongoDB queries by the URL path param `{rid}` directly (effectively `find({retailer_id: rid})`) without first verifying that `user.entity_id == rid OR user.role in {manufacturer/super_admin}`. The /customers route DOES have this guard — most others don't. Result: any authenticated retailer can enumerate any other retailer's data simply by changing the path param.
p0_cross_tenant_retailer_reads.mitigation: Create `def _assert_caller_owns_retailer(rid: str, user: dict)` that raises HTTPException(403, 'Forbidden — not your retailer') unless user['entity_id']==rid or user['role'] in {'super_admin','manufacturer','distributor','wholesaler'} (with the latter three only when they own this retailer via hierarchy). Apply via Depends() to every /api/retailer/{rid}/* read route. For /api/inventory, when `owner_type='retailer'`, apply the same guard against `owner_id`.
